title: Anthropic Has a $65 Billion Run Rate. Buy These Stocks to Profit From It.
author: Matthew Benjamin
description: Anthropic, operator of the Claude chatbot, has achieved a $65 billion annualized revenue run rate and plans to go public via IPO potentially valuing it at $2 trillion or more. Since Anthropic is not yet public, retail investors can gain indirect exposure through publicly traded companies that hold significant stakes in the AI firm, including Amazon (21%), Alphabet (15%), Salesforce, and Zoom Communications.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Amazon holds a 21% stake in Anthropic worth $33 billion. If Anthropic's IPO values the company at $2 trillion or more, Amazon shareholders would benefit significantly from the revaluation of this investment, similar to past gains from Space Exploration Technologies.

Alphabet holds a 15% stake in Anthropic and would benefit from a successful IPO valuation. However, sentiment is tempered by the fact that the stock has underperformed in 2026 due to investor concerns about AI infrastructure ROI.

title: Should You Buy Salesforce Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
author: Parkev Tatevosian, Cfa
description: Salesforce faces threats from substitute AI technology as the CRM company prepares for a major quarterly earnings report. CEO Marc Benioff spent a record $27 billion on stock buybacks in a single quarter to combat what he calls the 'SaaSpocalypse,' while the stock has fallen over 30% in 2026. Benioff maintains that Wall Street's fears about AI killing Salesforce are unfounded.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company faces significant headwinds including a 30% stock decline in 2026, threats from substitute AI technology, and the need for massive $27 billion buybacks to support the stock price. These defensive measures suggest underlying business concerns despite management's optimistic statements.

title: Marc Benioff's Salesforce Spent a Record $27 Billion on Stock Buybacks in a Single Quarter to Fight What He Calls the "SaaSpocalypse." Here's Why the Size of That Repurchase Matters.
author: John Ballard
description: Salesforce executed a record $27 billion stock buyback in Q1 (19% of market cap), signaling management confidence despite a 46% stock decline amid 'SaaSpocalypse' fears. The company's AI product Agentforce is scaling rapidly with $1.2B ARR (up 205% YoY) and surging usage metrics, suggesting AI is strengthening rather than disrupting the business. Total revenue beat consensus at $11B (+13% YoY) with strong free cash flow of $6.6B.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite stock decline of 46% from highs, the company demonstrated strong confidence through record $27B buyback, robust revenue growth of 13% YoY, exceptional Agentforce adoption (205% ARR growth, 152% QoQ token increase), and strong free cash flow of $6.6B. Management's conviction that AI strengthens rather than disrupts the business, combined with measurable product momentum, supports positive outlook.

title: C3.ai vs. Salesforce: Which Software Stock Pursuing Artificial Intelligence Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The article compares C3.ai and Salesforce as AI-focused software investments. C3.ai faces significant challenges with a 35.7% revenue decline, $470.4M net loss, negative free cash flow, and customer concentration risk. Salesforce demonstrates strong fundamentals with $41.5B revenue (+9.6% YoY), $7.5B net income, and robust AI product adoption ($3.4B ARR for Agentforce). The author recommends Salesforce as the better buy due to superior financial health and business momentum despite both stocks declining in 2026.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company experiencing severe financial distress with 35.7% revenue decline, $470.4M net loss, negative $190.7M free cash flow, $1.8B accumulated deficit, heavy customer concentration risk, and CEO transition uncertainty. Forward P/E of 25.6x indicates expensive valuation relative to poor fundamentals.

Strong financial performance with $41.5B revenue (+9.6% YoY), $7.5B net income (18% margin), $14.4B free cash flow, and robust AI adoption with $3.4B ARR for Agentforce products (+200% YoY). title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Is the Better Long-Term Investment?
author: Rick Orford
description: Salesforce offers a stronger valuation while ServiceNow has demonstrated more convincing evidence that enterprises will pay for AI workflow software. The key question is whether billings will reaccelerate in the fall, which would serve as a decisive test of growth, monetization, and investor confidence for both companies.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Salesforce is noted for offering a stronger valuation compared to ServiceNow, but lacks evidence of strong AI monetization, suggesting a balanced but less compelling investment thesis relative to its competitor.

ServiceNow has delivered more convincing evidence that enterprises will pay for AI workflow software, demonstrating stronger execution and better positioning in the AI software market, though valuation is less attractive than Salesforce.
